decisions.reason: Although it builds on the firm's wafer-processing know-how, its disappearance from the website after 2019 suggests weak commercial traction, and a focused firm would likely redeploy resources from this related but apparently underperforming variant.

This carrier wafer is technically close to the core business, but the lack of later visibility and the firm's stated move toward thinner and larger-format solutions make this smaller-diameter niche a plausible candidate for discontinuation.

As a flagship packaging-related innovation that extends existing glass-wafer capabilities and can be improved through the firm's own R&D and project experience, it fits the firm's absorptive capacity and strategic direction well enough to justify continued support.

An off-the-shelf glass and quartz wafer brand is extremely close to the firm's established knowledge base and commercialization channels, so management would be inclined to retain and scale it rather than exit it.

Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's established substrate and wafer-handling competences, so despite some material overlap the firm is unlikely to absorb and commercialize this line as effectively as its core products.
